{{Quote|We're not talking about a herd of murra on the prairies here&hellip;|[[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman Tagge]]|<ref name="Evasive Action: End Game">''[[Evasive Action: End Game]]''</ref>}}
'''Murra''' were a tall [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Goat/Legends|goat-like]] [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]] [[Diet/Legends|herbivores]] native to the flat [[Grass/Legends|grasslands]] of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia's]] northern continent, though species of murra also inhabited the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] and [[Forest/Legends|forest]] regions. Slow-witted and incredibly strong, murra were raised by [[Farmer/Legends|ranchers]] for their [[Foodstuff/Legends|meat]], for their thick hides, and as beasts of burden. A murra had large, curved tusks growing from their lower jaw, and two long horns that swept backwards from the crown of its blunt head. [[Kahmurra]], found on the [[Double Worlds|Double World]] of [[Talus/Legends|Talus]], were a distant relative of the murra, [[Gene/Legends|genetically]] [[Bioengineering/Legends|engineered]] as a possible all-terrain [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]] beast.

==Biology and appearance==
The [[Diet/Legends|herbivorous]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Limb/Legends|quadrupedal]] [[vertebrate]] [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]] known as murra<ref name="AED" /> were native to the [[Grass/Legends|grasslands]] of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia's]] northern continent,<ref name="Suns">''[[Suns of Fortune]]''</ref> a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Galactic Core]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> However, the [[Goat/Legends|goat-like]] species also inhabited [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] and [[Forest/Legends|forest]] regions of Corellia. A group of murra was referred to as a pack.<ref name="AED" /> Slow-witted and incredibly strong, murra had thick,<ref name="Suns" /> [[Color/Legends|brown-colored]] hides, orange [[Eye/Legends|eyes]],<ref name="AED" /> large, curved tusks growing from their lower jaws, and two long horns that swept backwards from the crown of its blunt head. The murra's hide was thick yet supple, and covered with a dense mat of stout, course [[Hair/Legends|hairs]] like the bristles of a scrubbing brush. Despite their fearsome looks, murra were quite docile and biddable.<ref name="Suns" /> This was unlike their [[Gene/Legends|genetically]] [[Bioengineering/Legends|engineered]] distant relatives, the [[kahmurra]], bred for their viciousness.<ref name="AED" /> Murra had a slow, plodding gait that they could maintain over many [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] of rough terrain, and they could haul or pull loads well out of scale with their stature. Though not aggressive, murra could spook easily, and if startled would kick or lash out with their horns. Entire herds of murra, often frightened by loud noises or storms, were known to stampede en mass, causing incredible amounts of damage as they went.<ref name="Suns" /> When vocalizing, they would emit a deep growling noise.<ref name="AED" />

==History==
{{Quote|A former Imperial scientist was working in a bio-genetics lab on Talus. He was in charge of genetic experiments aiming to transform the goat-like murra from Corellia into an efficient all-terrain fighting animal. The resulting creature was named a kahmurra, though the Empire considered it a failure and cancelled all funding.|[[Yondalla]], to a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]]|<ref name="SWG:Y">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=other|Corellian Corvette Pre-Quest: "Yondalla"}}</ref>}}
Murra could be tamed or incubated by [[Beastmaster/Legends|beast masters]], and [[Farmer/Legends|ranchers]] were known to raise murra for their [[Foodstuff/Legends|meat]], for their thick hides, and as beasts of burden. During the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]],<ref name="AED" /> [[Borvo]] the Hutt possessed several murra which [[Gender/Legends|he]] used to defend his [[Borvo's Vault|vault]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="SWG:ORDMBBD">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Old Republic Droid Modules: Borvo's Battle Droid|Naboo}}</ref> On the [[Double Worlds|Double World]] of [[Talus/Legends|Talus]], the [[Kahmurra Biogenetic Research Station]] was used by the Galactic Empire to genetically engineer murra into a more efficient all-terrain fighting animal. The resulting creature was named a kahmurra (or sometimes khmurra), though the Empire considered the project a failure and cancelled all funding. Kahmurra had since run wild on Talus, with some being caught and trained, though with great difficulty.<ref name="AED" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Murra_concept_art.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Concept art for ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]''.]]
[[W:c:swg:Murra|Murra]] first appeared as [[W:c:swg:Creatures & enemies|creatures]] in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], a [[Roleplaying game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]], prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="AED" /><ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> There also existed other named types of murra, including the forest murra and mountain murra. However, each of these murra were virtually identical in size and appearance to a typical murra, so it is not clear whether they constituted distinct subspecies, or were merely descriptive names for different types of the same creature.<ref name="AED" />

With the release of [[W:c:swg:Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies'']], murra could be [[W:c:swg:Tame (Ability)|tamed]] as [[W:c:swg:Pets|pets]] by players who pursued the [[W:c:swg:Creature Handler|creature handler]] [[W:c:swg:Professions (pre-NGE)|profession]].<ref name="AED" /> Following the release of [[W:c:swg:Publish 25 Notes for November 15 2005|Publish 25's]] [[W:c:swg:New Game Enhancements|New Game Enhancements]] on [[November 15]], [[2005]], creature handlers were removed.<ref name="AED" /><ref name="NGE">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64886&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2005}}</ref> However, with the release of [[W:c:swg:Chapter 6 Notes for May 22 2007|Chapter 6: Masters of the Wild]] on [[May 22]], [[2007]], [[W:c:swg:Beast Master|beast masters]] were added as an [[W:c:swg:Expertise|expertise]] path,<ref name="Chapter6">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66959&resource=publish#chapter6|text=Chapter 6: Masters of the Wild}}</ref> allowing players to incubate creatures as pets.<ref name="AED" /> ''[[Suns of Fortune]]'', an official rules supplement published on [[January 24]], [[2014]], describes some features of the murra in greater detail. However, it also presents something of a discrepancy. The sourcebook claims that the murra had four large tusks growing from its lower jaw,<ref name="Suns" /> while ''Star Wars Galaxies'' only depicted two.<ref name="AED" />
